title: Exceptional inverse image of a smooth morphism commutes with extension of coefficients
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: $k$ has characteristic $p>0$, $\ell\ne p$ is prime, and $X,Y$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Fix its coefficient-independent compactification. Let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings, each annihilated by a power of $\ell$. Write $\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},R)$ for complexes of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $R_T$ with bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Use derived coefficient extension $K_B=K\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], the constructible adjunctions $Rf_{!,R}\dashv f_R^!$ for $R=A,B$ [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation], and the canonical compact-support comparison $b$ [det-sp-reduction-direct-image]. For a common annihilator $N=\ell^n$ of $A,B$, the Tate line is the inverse image from the etale site of $\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}R_T$; write $K(d)=K\otimes^L_R R_T(1)^{\otimes d}$ [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist].

For
$K\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ let

$$
c_{A,B}(K):(f_A^!K)_B\longrightarrow f_B^!(K_B)\quad\text{in }\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},B)
$$

be the unique morphism (the transpose under $Rf_{!,B}\dashv f_B^!$) satisfying

$$
\varepsilon_B(K_B)\circ Rf_{!,B}\bigl(c_{A,B}(K)\bigr)
=(\varepsilon_A(K))_B\circ b(f_A^!K)^{-1}.
$$

Then $c_{A,B}(K)$ is natural in $K$ and is an isomorphism. On a coordinate
chart $f|_U=p_d\circ e$ (with $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_Y$ étale and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ is the chart inclusion, where
$j^*f_A^!\simeq e^*p_d^*(-)(d)[2d]$ is the counit-preserving identification for the chart adjunction whose counit is summation over the fibres of $e$ followed by the affine-space counit of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], transported from the etale site) it is the canonical isomorphism
$(e^*p_d^*K(d)[2d])_B\simeq e^*p_d^*(K_B)(d)[2d]$.

proof.text: Put $F_R=Rf_{!,R}$, $G_R=f_R^!$ and $T=(-)_B$. By [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation] and [det-sp-reduction-direct-image], $T\epsilon_A\,b(G_A-)^{-1}$ is well typed. Define $c$ by transposition. The adjunction hom bijection gives its displayed counit identity and uniqueness. Naturality of $b,\epsilon_A$ gives naturality of its inverse transpose, hence of $c$.

Choose affine source/base charts by [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form], composing with the open base-change inclusion $\mathbf A^d_V\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^d_Y$; this stays etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Pure dimension fixes $d$. Standing schemes are Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; open charts are qc and finite type [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian, lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. The etale map is finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). Its diagonal is a base change of the closed $k$-diagonal of the source [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b), so it is separated.

The normalized projective-line splitting and counit equations are [lem-sp-p1-splitting-scalar] and [lem-sp-p1-counit-scalar]. On $g=p_de$, apply [lem-sp-affine-counit-scalar] and [lem-sp-etale-sum-counit-scalar]. Mate pasting [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2) makes their composite right map the canonical tensor isomorphism $a_g$, with coefficient-counit identity. The normalization of [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization] preserves the sum counit; the composition and refinement squares of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] identify the pasted left map with the fixed-compactification $\beta_g$.

All chart functors restrict to the finite-Tor categories by [lem-sp-etale-ctf-chart-domain]. Transport their adjunctions by [det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer], retaining $\epsilon_g^{pro}=\nu^*\epsilon_g^{et}c_g^{-1}$. The first square and counit clause of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] turn the preceding identity into $T\epsilon_{g,A}b_g^{-1}=\epsilon_{g,B}Rg_{!,B}(a_g)$. Thus $a_g$ is the named pro-etale mate.

source.place: Charts: transport of the normalized counit

proof.text: For the chart inclusion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, [det-sf-mate-open-restriction] identifies $j^*G_R$ with $G_{fj,R}$, counit-preservingly for [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. As $j$ is separated etale of finite type with at most one summand, [lem-sp-etale-sum-counit-scalar] gives its etale coefficient-counit identity; transported as in Step 4 by [lem-sp-etale-ctf-chart-domain] and [det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer], the mate of $b_j^{-1}$ is the canonical restriction/tensor map $a_j$. The composition square in [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] gives $b_{fj}=F_{f,B}(b_j)b_f(j_{!,A}-)$. Mate pasting [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2) gives $c_{fj}=G_{j,B}(c_f)a_j(G_{f,A}-)$, i.e. $j^*c_f=c_{fj}$, and Step 4 with uniqueness of transposes gives $j^*c_f=a_g$. Charts cover $X$, and [det-sf-mate-open-restriction](3) detects invertibility.

source.place: Locality: open restriction and final assembly

split_report.blueprint: Existence, uniqueness, naturality is Step 1; Charts is Steps 2–4 through the finite-Tor domain, Kummer splitting, P1 counit, etale sum counit and ordered affine induction helper proofs; Locality is Step 5. The unit route and every clause of the item are unchanged.

tool_uses.why: The coefficient extension and associativity definition is part of the reduction unit itself and types all coefficient changes.
Supplies the restricted right-adjoint Hom bijections for arbitrary finite ell-primary rings; the unit chart statement only has Zn coefficients.
Supplies the canonical b from the first half of the same coefficient-comparison unit, including arbitrary nonflat coefficient maps.
Generic smooth-coordinate existence, used only to supply the charts on which the unit instructs us to check c.
Generic Noetherian permanence used to check the geometric hypotheses of ordinary finite-ring P1 adjunctions.
Generic open Noetherian permanence, ensuring quasi-compact finite-type open restrictions meet the chart adjunction hypotheses.
Generic finite-type criterion for the chosen open charts, used in geometric admissibility checks.
Generic finite-presentation criterion for affine-source etale coordinate maps, checking their compact-support domain.
Generic closed-immersion base-change permanence, used to prove separatedness of each etale coordinate map by its relative diagonal.
Existing Mathlib leaf, clause (2), identifies the mate of a square pasted along consecutive adjunctions; its specialization replaces the hidden general composite-counit lemma.
Generic identification of the compactification candidate for a separated etale chart map with exact sum extension, preserving the counit; needed to identify the chart composite with Rg_! (Step 8).
Existing normalized site/coefficient, etale-sum, composition and refinement squares identify every chart calculation with the named compact-support map.
Generic transport of an adjunction retaining its actual counit, required to compare the etale chart computation with the pro-etale right adjoint.
Generic counit-preserving source-open restriction of f! and open-cover isomorphism detection; the reduction unit has no separate locality theorem.
Generic formula for units, counits and Hom bijections of composite adjunctions, used to write out rather than assume scalar/restriction compatibility.
